title: Introduce heterogeneous metadata normalizer and bandwidth-savvy profile summarizer
author: Anika Bose
release_notes: Adds a metadata normalizer that canonicalizes heterogeneous onboarding keys and introduces a compact, bandwidth-aware performance profile summarizer plus a changelog seed generator for concise release briefs.
description:
Motivation and summary: We often onboard models with inconsistent metadata keys (eg: 'vocab_size' vs 'vocabSize', variant labels that mix hardware hints and quantization tags, and nested provenance blobs). This PR adds a lightweight, configurable metadata-normalizer pipeline that canonicalizes incoming model metadata into stable keys for the registry, plus a compact 'bandwidth-savvy' profile summarizer that prioritizes metrics relevant to networked inference (token throughput vs serialized package size). The change also wires a small changelog-seed generator that produces terse, draft release notes from the normalized metadata and profile deltas so maintainers get a one-click starting point for release briefs.

What this PR contains (single-string description of changes and rationale): implemented normalizer rules (case-folding, underscore/camelCase mapping, canonical tag map for known keys like architecture, quantization, tokenizer, provenance), introduced a plugin hook for tenant-specific normalization overrides (used by tests to simulate enterprise variant), added a compact profile summarizer that computes: median p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, serialized weight size, kv-cache memory footprint, and a derived 'bandwidth-impact' score (heuristic: serialized_size * tokens/sec normalized by model family). The summarizer outputs an abridged JSON line designed for quick dashboarding and for the changelog seed generator. The changelog seed synthesizes bullet points for new model versions by diffing normalized metadata and summarizer output against the previous release, and emits prioritized bullets (breaking-affects, performance-regressions, noteworthy latency/cost improvements).

Commits (high-level): - Add normalizer core and canonical mapping table (anika/normalize-core) - Add tenant override mechanism and tests (anika/normalize-overrides) - Implement bandwidth-savvy summarizer and unit tests (anika/profile-summarizer) - Add changelog seed generator and simple CLI preview (anika/changelog-seed) - Integration tests & registry wiring + docs (anika/integration-docs)

Files/areas changed (high level): - registry/normalizer/{core.py, rules.py, canonical_map.yaml, README.md} - registry/profiles/{summarizer.py, bandwidth_score.py, tests/} - registry/changelog/seed_generator.py - tools/cli/changelog_preview.py - docs/model-onboarding-normalization.md - tests/integration/test_normalizer_end_to_end.py

Design notes and constraints: - Normalizer is intentionally conservative: it never discards unknown keys, it only adds canonical aliases and writes a normalized top-level object while retaining original raw metadata field under raw_metadata for auditability. - Tenant overrides are applied as an ordered patch to the canonical_map.yaml and validated by the same rule engine to avoid silent collisions. - Bandwidth-impact heuristic is flagged as implementation detail (non-breaking) and surfaced with confidence buckets (low/medium/high) so downstream consumers can opt-in.

Checklist: - [x] Normalizer core implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] Tenant override hook & validation tests - [x] Bandwidth summarizer implemented with unit tests - [x] Changelog seed generator with basic diff heuristics - [x] Integration test that wires normalized output into changelog preview - [x] Docs and usage notes for maintainers - [x] Performance sanity: normalizer adds <2ms median overhead for typical metadata payloads (measured in microbenchmarks included)

Review conversation (summarized): - Diego: "Can we avoid duplicating synonyms across canonical_map.yaml and registry's legacy aliases?" Response: "Yes — added a migration helper that folds legacy aliases into the canonical map and a small enforcement test to prevent divergence." - Rachel: "How do we prevent false-positive breaking notes from trivial metadata formatting changes?" Response: "Changelog seed now filters formatting-only diffs (case/sep changes) by comparing normalized values rather than raw keys; also added confidence buckets and a 'suggested' tag rather than auto-publish." - Omar: "Is bandwidth-impact explainable for SREs?" Response: "Added an explanation block in the summarizer output including contributing factors and a reproducible formula; also documented recommended thresholds for alerting in docs." - Diego requested a small refactor to make canonical_map lookups O(1) for large onboarding batches; addressed by memoizing map lookups and added benchmark.

CI and validation notes: Initial CI run had a lint failure related to line length in docs; fixed. Integration tests initially flaked in CI due to ephemeral registry DB lock; added retry/backoff to the test harness. Final CI status: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, typecheck).

Backward compatibility and migration: Normalizer is opt-in at registry ingestion; existing model entries are not mass-migrated. We included a migration tool (scripts/migrate_normalized_snapshots.py) that operators can run to backfill normalized keys for a chosen namespace. The changelog seed generator respects unnormalized entries by falling back to raw_metadata diffs where no normalized counterpart exists.

Operational considerations: - Documented how to add tenant overrides and how to pin a model's canonical keyset when performing rollbacks. - Added a lightweight metric (registry.normalizer.latency_ms) and a counter for normalization failures for SRE to monitor.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged. Reason: small-focus feature set, cleaner linear history for changelog seed semantics. Merged by: Diego Martens.

Follow-ups (planned): - Add a small UI in registry console to preview normalized metadata and proposed changelog bullets (UX: ENG-2102). - Expand bandwidth-impact formula to include request-level batching patterns (ENG-2199). - Add an opt-in nightly job to propose backfill candidates and PR drafts for maintainers.

Related work: references to existing model registry PRs and utilities that inspired parts of this change (profiling heuristics, changelog diffs, canonical tagging) are linked in the docs file above. For any questions ping @anika or link to Linear ENG-1987 for design notes.
notes: This PR purposefully keeps the normalizer non-destructive and provides operator tooling for migration; it is intended to reduce churn when teams submit model metadata with divergent conventions. The changelog seed should not be treated as authoritative until maintainers review and edit the generated bullets.
